headline: Roman has new evening confusion (including leaving the stove on), a drop of about 8.6% in body weight over 12 weeks, and a decline in bathing and dressing independence.

items.statement: On 2026-11-09 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. He was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, a medication review and a PCP visit that week. No results or PCP follow-up are in the evidence.
items.verifier_note: The 11-09 nursing note contains every detail. The empty encounters record is consistent with the statement that no results or PCP follow-up are in the evidence.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 2026-09-05 to 75.2 kg on 2026-11-24 (-7.1 kg, -8.6%), with intermediate readings of 79.8 kg on 10-01 and 77.3 kg on 10-28. He reports poor appetite and skips breakfast, and he eats about 50% of day center lunches. The dietitian planned an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record supports all four weights and the -7.1 kg / -8.6% change. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast, 50% lunch intake and the plan.

items.statement: On 2026-09-18 he needed hands-on help getting out of the tub and said he has been skipping showers because he fears slipping. On 2026-09-25 OT found he now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, where he was independent at the last review. OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The 09-18 aide note and the 09-25 OT note support every detail, including independence at the last review and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-24 PT found his gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use, and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see him twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: The 10-24 PT note supports the gait findings, the TUG of 19 seconds, the recommendations and the twice-weekly sessions.

questions_for_team: Have the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-09 been done, and what did they show?
What interim safety plan is there for the stove and for evenings at home while the confusion is being evaluated?
Have the OT and PT equipment recommendations (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, walker, grab bars) and the increased home care hours been ordered or approved?
Is the weight loss being evaluated beyond the dietitian's plan, and how will the weekly weights be reviewed?
Could the confusion, poor appetite and decline in function be related, and who coordinates the follow-up across disciplines?

bleeding bruising dark stool hemoglobin CBC anemia
HbA1c glucose lipid panel LDL cholesterol lab results

IDT action items prior meeting caregiver niece Linda transportation pain management

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the last IDT review/enrollment baseline (enrolled 2024-10-07) is the comparison point; note any gap in documentation covering the window.

Falls and near-falls: count and circumstances since last review, injuries, and whether any fall occurred on or related to chronic pain, knee osteoarthritis, or fibromyalgia symptoms; check fall-risk screen and assistive device use.

ED visits and hospital admissions/observation stays since last review: reasons, discharge summaries, and any follow-up appointments that were missed or completed; pay particular attention to chest pain, ischemic heart disease, or COPD/bronchitis exacerbations.

Cardiac and respiratory symptoms: documented chest pain or nitroglycerin spray use, dyspnea, cough/sputum change, oxygen use, and rescue inhaler use; note any new urgent-care or antibiotic/steroid courses for bronchitis.

Medication changes: reconcile active list (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, naproxen, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) against the window; identify any new starts, stops, dose changes, refills missed, or pharmacy gaps. Flag for prescriber review: naproxen use alongside clopidogrel and hypertension/ischemic heart disease, and whether naproxen is still intended.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including any readings above or below targets, orthostatic symptoms, and whether metoprolol timing or dosing changed.

Weight and BMI trend (obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes): recorded weights, direction and magnitude of change, and most recent glucose/HbA1c and lipid results with dates; check whether labs are due.
Anemia and bleeding risk: most recent hemoglobin/CBC, any reported bleeding, dark stools, or bruising given antiplatelet therapy and NSAID use; flag whether a repeat CBC is due or overdue.

Pain and function: pain scores, chronic pain/low back pain/fibromyalgia management changes, ADL and IADL status (bathing, dressing, transfers, mobility, medication management, meal prep), and any decline in function since last review.

Cognition, mood, and engagement: any screening results (cognitive, depression such as PHQ), reported low mood, isolation, sleep changes, and PACE center or day-program attendance rate in the window including missed days and reasons.

Caregiver and social situation: changes in living arrangement, caregiver availability or strain, transportation barriers, housing or financial concerns, and any caregiver-reported concerns to raise with the team.

Care-plan items due or overdue: preventive screenings and vaccines (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID, zoster), eye/foot exams relevant to metabolic conditions, osteoarthritis or pain reassessment, advance directive and code status review, and any open IDT action items from the prior meeting with their status.

Summarize for the IDT: list what changed in the window (new events, med changes, trends, function, attendance), prioritize items needing clinician discussion, and mark data gaps or conflicting documentation for the team to resolve rather than making treatment recommendations.
